headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of increasing electric generating capacity and new distribution infrastructure to large energy users, including data centers, to reduce residential electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Dominion Energy (initially supported original bill).
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users, Governor Spanberger (due to amendments).
news_headline: Virginia governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics argue the governor's amendments weakened the original intent of the bill, particularly regarding the allocation of capacity market costs to data centers.

headline: Data Centers Report Water Use
short_summary: This bill requires water users supplying data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption data, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for transparency and planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local communities, Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ).
news_headline: Environmental Impact Measures Advance Through Legislature
news_summary: Virginia policymakers passed legislation, including SB 553, to gain clarity into how much water data centers use, requiring water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers monthly or quarterly. This aims to enhance transparency, oversight, and planning for water resources given the significant water consumption by data centers.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including noise profiles and potential impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests, to inform siting decisions.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, historic preservation advocates, farmland protection groups.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, commercial real estate associations.
news_headline: What does Data center site assessment and sound profile for high energy use facilities (HB153) do?
news_summary: HB 153 requires Virginia local governments to review potential impacts before approving new data centers using 100 megawatts or more, mandating site assessments for noise and other environmental factors. This helps localities make informed decisions that align with community plans and zoning rules, though expansions under 100 megawatts are exempt.
